stats.label: Time spent on admin-related scheduling tasks

blocks.text: Setting up your Gmail environment on Mac

Since there is no native Gmail app for macOS, you should create a dedicated web app. Open Gmail in Safari and go to File > Add to Dock. This creates a standalone icon in your Dock. It keeps your inbox separate from your general browsing tabs. You can also use Chrome to do this by selecting the three-dot menu, then Save and Share > Install page as app.

Speed is vital when you process hundreds of emails. Go to Settings > General > Keyboard shortcuts to turn them on. Once enabled, press Shift + / to see the full list. Use c to compose, e to archive, and r to reply. These small movements save hours over a week of candidate outreach.

Organization prevents candidate data from slipping through the cracks. Create labels for each stage of your hiring funnel. Use labels like In Review, Interview Scheduled, and Offer Sent. You can color code these labels in the left sidebar. Right-click a label to select a color that stands out. This visual cue helps you spot high-priority emails instantly.
Use the search bar to find emails with attachments. Type has:attachment in the search box to filter your inbox. This is helpful when looking for resumes sent by candidates.
blocks.title: Quick search tip

blocks.text: Recruitment coordinators often send the same emails repeatedly. Use templates to save time. Go to Settings > Advanced and enable Templates. Once enabled, click the three-dot menu in the compose window to save your current draft as a template. You can insert these with one click when responding to common candidate questions.

Scheduling interviews consumes nearly half of a coordinator's day. Minimize this by using a booking link in your signature. Ensure your calendar is synced correctly with your Gmail account. If you need to manually schedule, use the snooze feature to follow up with candidates who have not responded to your interview request.

Lazur helps you stay focused while you work in Gmail. Hold Option + Command to ask Lazur about your screen. It can explain how to set up a filter or point at the correct menu item for your settings. You can also use it to draft responses to candidates quickly.

items: Forgetting to enable keyboard shortcuts, which slows down your workflow.
Keeping too many tabs open instead of using a dedicated web app.
Ignoring the daily sending limit, which can lead to a 24-hour block.
Failing to use filters to separate candidate emails from internal team messages.
Not using the Undo Send feature to catch errors in interview details.

blocks.text: If you send mass emails to candidates, be aware of the daily limits. Personal accounts are limited to 500 recipients per day. Workspace accounts allow up to 2,000. These limits apply to the total number of recipients across all your emails. Exceeding these limits stops you from sending mail for 24 hours. Plan your outreach accordingly to avoid disruption.

faq.question: Is there a native Gmail app for Mac?
faq.answer: No, Google does not provide a native Gmail application for macOS. You can create a web app using the Add to Dock feature in Safari or the Install as app option in Chrome.

faq.question: How do I make Gmail faster on my Mac?
faq.answer: Enable keyboard shortcuts in your Gmail settings and use a dedicated web app to keep your inbox organized and separate from your browser tabs.

faq.question: What is the daily email sending limit for Gmail?
faq.answer: Personal Gmail accounts can send to up to 500 recipients per day, while Google Workspace accounts support up to 2,000 recipients.
